title.narrative: Enhancing Access to Lifesaving Integrated SRH, SGBV, and MHPSS Services for Women, Girls, and Vulnerable Populations in Areas at Risk of Famine

description.narrative: The project aims to improve access to life-saving, multi-sectoral, integrated sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender-based violence (GBV) services for approximately 43,000 beneficiaries in areas at risk of famine over a nine-month period. Targeted locations include:North Darfur: Tawila, El Fasher and BelielSouth Darfur: Nyala Jenoubi and Nyala ShemalEast Darfur: El FardosNorth Kordofan: SheikanSouth Kordofan: KadugliWest Darfur: Forbarange, Sirba, KereneikCentral Darfur: Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) clusterKhartoum: Jabal AwliyaThe project will enhance SRH service delivery by offering clinical management of rape (CMR), HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) treatment, family planning, and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). This will be achieved through the deployment of mobile and temporary clinics, maintenance of ambulances for emergency referrals, support for Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (EmONC) facilities, deployment of healthcare providers, activation of state-level SRH Working Groups, and provision of emergency cash assistance for normal deliveries, caesarean sections, and obstetric complications.In parallel, the project will improve the safety, health, and well-being of women and girls by establishing and supporting Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS), offering confidential, survivor-centered services, and conducting community awareness sessions on GBV and available support services. It will also establish community-based protection networks (CBPNs), including youth-led CBPNs, to facilitate timely interventions. Additionally, cash for case management and vouchers for sanitary items will be provided.To identify and mitigate GBV risks, the project will conduct refresher training for service providers on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), perform safety audits and assessments, and organize advocacy meetings with local leaders and armed groups to ensure access to essential health and protection services.
